Subject: Procurement path & next steps (Acme)

Hi Samantha / Tom -

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Summary of discussion
- Use case: Acme search & customer support assistant (approx 2M tokens/day peak).
- Priority: low-latency inference for customer-facing flows, SLOs ~ <200ms 95th.
- Data controls: needs VPC/private deployment for some PII workflows.

2) Procurement / commercial items we covered
- Pricing model: usage-based (tokens) for hosted, reserved commit for Dedicated.
- Payment: PO accepted (net-30) or credit card; Marketplace listing would allow card and faster procurement - you mentioned Procurement prefers PO.
- Contract: standard Redwood SaaS agreement + DPA; can sign via DocuSign.

3) Immediate asks / next steps
- Samantha: confirm who the economic buyer / budget owner is, and whether Procurement needs an SOW or paperwork up front.
- Tom: confirm whether Acme will route via Cloud Marketplace (AWS) or direct PO.
- Marissa/Vivek/Aditya: we will prepare a draft SOW and a short procurement packet (pricing sheet, SOC2 excerpt, privacy sheet).

Attached: draft SOW (initial), Redwood privacy summary. Happy to hop on a short call with Procurement if helpful.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Economic buyer / budget owner: this sits with Product (Elena Martinez). Finance is the sponsor (Raj Patel). Final signatory for contracts above $100k is our VP of Procurement (CFO signs for >$250k) - Procurement looped here can confirm thresholds.
- We prefer PO for 90% of vendors. Card is only for < $5k purchases.
- Marketplace: we are evaluating marketplace procurement for some SaaS, but for vendor-dependent infra we tend to prefer a direct PO so we retain contractual controls. That said, if Redwood is on AWS Marketplace in the near term that could speed purchase for a pilot.

Procurement: can you confirm the standard lead time you need for an SOW + PO? Also need SOC2 and a short list of data handling controls.

I'll schedule a quick 15-min sync with Elena and Raj if helpful - tentatively Thu 10am PT.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director, Product Operations | Acme Corp

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement path & next steps (Acme)

Hi Samantha - great context, thanks. Short answers to Procurement questions: 

- Lead time: for a standard SOW + PO we typically turn around a draft SOW + pricing sheet in 2 business days once scope is locked. Legal review time varies; many customers see a 7-14 day cycle for initial PO acceptance.
- Data controls: attaching a one-page security summary and SOC2 excerpt (see attachments from Marissa). We can provide more detail or a completed security questionnaire if Procurement requires it.
- Marketplace option: being on AWS Marketplace allows for consolidated billing and often speeds approvals, but it does add some constraints on invoicing cadence. If you prefer direct PO for contractual control, we're happy to proceed that way.

Regarding signatory path and thresholds, happy to be on the call with Elena and Raj to map the internal approval route and provide any supplemental materials Procurement will want.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
